intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 (DEE46) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GRIN2D gene (602717) on chromosome 19q13.33.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 (DEE46) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GRIN2D gene.
checks.evidence_quote: GRIN2D Recurrent De Novo Dominant Mutation Causes a Severe Epileptic Encephalopathy Treatable with NMDA Receptor Channel Blockers.
checks.explanation: The title and abstract say a heterozygous GRIN2D mutation causes epileptic encephalopathy. The DEE46 label is OMIM's name for this disorder.

checks.claim: The GRIN2D gene is located on chromosome 19q13.33.
checks.evidence_quote: a NMDAR gene previously unrecognized to harbor disease-causing mutations, GRIN2D
checks.explanation: The paper does not give the chromosomal location. Under the task rules, a gene's chromosomal location is standard nomenclature and counts as supported.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 is a severe neurologic disorder with seizures that are refractory to conventional antiepileptic medications (Li et al., 2016) and severe developmental delay (Tsuchida et al., 2018). The disorder is caused by de novo heterozygous mutation in GRIN2D, which encodes the GluN2D subunit of the NMDA-type glutamate receptor. Functional studies showed that the mutation increases receptor function (gain of function) (Li et al., 2016).

checks.evidence_quote: Causes a Severe Epileptic Encephalopathy
checks.explanation: The title calls the disorder a severe epileptic encephalopathy.

checks.claim: In developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46, seizures are refractory to conventional antiepileptic medications.
checks.evidence_quote: Because both individuals' seizures had proven refractory to conventional antiepileptic medications
checks.explanation: The abstract says both patients' seizures did not respond to conventional antiepileptic drugs.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 involves severe developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: novel heterozygous GRIN2D missense variants in three unrelated patients with severe developmental delay and intractable epilepsy
checks.explanation: Severe developmental delay is stated directly.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 is caused by de novo heterozygous mutation in GRIN2D.
checks.evidence_quote: we report a de novo recurrent heterozygous missense mutation-c.1999G>A (p.Val667Ile)-in a NMDAR gene previously unrecognized to harbor disease-causing mutations, GRIN2D
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a de novo heterozygous GRIN2D mutation.

checks.claim: GRIN2D encodes the GluN2D subunit of the NMDA-type glutamate receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: The resulting GluN2D p.Val667Ile exchange occurs in the M3 transmembrane domain involved in channel gating.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls GRIN2D an NMDAR gene and names its product GluN2D.

checks.claim: Functional studies showed that the GRIN2D mutation causing developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 increases receptor function (gain of function).
checks.evidence_quote: This gain-of-function mutation increases glutamate and glycine potency by 2-fold, increases channel open probability by 6-fold
checks.explanation: Functional studies showed a gain of function.

paragraphs.text: Li et al. (2016) used exome and candidate panel sequencing to study 2 unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy. Both carried the same de novo heterozygous missense mutation in the GRIN2D gene, val667-to-ile (V667I). In functional studies, NMDA receptors containing the mutant GluN2D subunit showed a 2-fold increase in glutamate and glycine potency, and Li et al. (2016) classified the mutation as gain-of-function. Li et al. (2016) also tested the sensitivity of the mutant receptors to FDA-approved NMDA receptor antagonists in vitro.

paragraphs.text: Li et al. (2016) based treatment on in vitro results showing that the mutant GRIN2D receptors were sensitive to FDA-approved NMDA receptor antagonists. Both children received oral memantine, and Li et al. (2016) reported mild to moderate improvement in seizure burden and development. The older proband later developed refractory status epilepticus and was treated with ketamine and magnesium.

paragraphs.text: Li et al. (2016) found a de novo heterozygous c.1999G-A transition in the GRIN2D gene in 2 unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy (DEE46). The mutation results in a val667-to-ile (V667I) substitution in the M3 transmembrane domain of GluN2D. Functional studies showed that the mutant receptors gained function, including a 2-fold increase in sensitivity to glutamate and glycine.

checks.explanation: The variant, zygosity, de novo status and both unrelated patients all match the abstract.
